slides.narration: Welcome to Book II, Chapter 11: Creating Generic Functions with Templates. This deck follows the Chapter 1 Slides model: concept on the left, code or evidence on the right, and presenter notes that tell the instructor what to say and do. Modern C++ is not about using the newest syntax because it looks impressive. It is about encoding ownership, lifetime, invariants, generic behavior, and failure boundaries so the program is easier to reason about and harder to misuse.

slides.title: 11.1 Defining Function Templates
keyPoints: A function template describes a family of functions parameterized by types or other template arguments.
The compiler forms suitable specializations when the program uses them.
The body still has requirements: every selected operation must be meaningful for the chosen type.
Write those requirements down even before expressing them through concepts.
slides.narration: In Book II, Chapter 11, treat 11.1 Defining Function Templates as a design decision with costs and evidence. A function template describes a family of functions parameterized by types or other template arguments. The compiler forms suitable specializations when the program uses them. The body still has requirements: every selected operation must be meaningful for the chosen type. Write those requirements down even before expressing them through concepts. An unconstrained template is not an algorithm that works for every conceivable type. slides.narration: In Book II, Chapter 11, treat 11.1.2 Understanding Template Argument Deduction as a design decision with costs and evidence. For larger(3, 9), deduction can select T as int. For two doubles it can select double. Mixed arguments such as an integer and a double do not automatically establish one agreed T under this simple signature; an explicit conversion or a different multi-parameter design is needed. Deduction does not inspect the function’s intended business meaning. It follows language rules for the parameter pattern and arguments. Read a deduction failure from the call outward: identify each candidate type, the conflicting positions, and whether a conversion should really be permitted. Broadening every parameter until a call compiles can weaken useful type distinctions. slides.narration: In Book II, Chapter 11, treat 11.2.2 Constraining Acceptable Types as a design decision with costs and evidence. The clamp template uses a type trait and static_assert to limit this lesson’s implementation to arithmetic types. It rejects inverted bounds at runtime. For floating-point inputs, its comparison logic assumes an ordered finite domain; NaN requires an additional policy because ordinary comparisons do not establish the expected interval relationships. A static assertion inside a template body is not the same as a C++20 constraint participating in candidate selection. It can still yield a useful diagnostic after instantiation, but concepts express eligibility more directly. Chapter 13 develops that distinction and combines type-level requirements with value-level overflow checks. slides.narration: In Book II, Chapter 11, treat Evidence and interpretation as a design decision with costs and evidence. The integer comparison returns nine, the double comparison returns 2.5, and the C-string call returns the owning string beta. Clamp maps twelve to ten, minus one to zero, and five to itself. Inverted bounds throw before a clamped value is returned. The text overload is important because a syntactically available pointer comparison would not express lexical content ordering. Generic correctness has both syntactic and semantic layers: a compiler can verify that an expression exists without proving that it means what the application intends. slides.narration: In Book II, Chapter 11, treat Failure clinic — Generic syntax, wrong semantics as a design decision with costs and evidence. The naïve text template compares two C-string pointer values. It compiles for many calls, but it does not express lexicographic ordering of the characters. The repair is to adapt the representation to a text value or view with the intended comparison semantics. Adding more template parameters does not solve the domain mismatch. Another failure appears at link time because a template definition was placed in a source file without providing the needed explicit instantiation. A declaration allows the caller to form a call, but the complete program still needs the selected specialization’s definition. Either make the definition available where instantiation occurs or intentionally manage a fixed set of instantiations in the build.
